source.title: Examining the Causal Structures of Deep Neural Networks Using Information Theory
source.authors: Scythia Marrow; Eric J. Michaud; Erik P. Hoel

record.file_problem: none; supplied text includes the article and supplementary information
record.tranche_reason: The study measures causal-structure properties during training and relates their trajectories to training and testing performance, but does not directly test the listed memorization, architecture, optimizer, batch-size, regularization, sharpness, or example-removal claims.
record.gate_note: The study reports training and testing loss curves alongside effective-information measurements for Iris and reduced-MNIST networks. These results bear on V7's claim that measured properties of trained networks track the training–test gap. The paper does not report the magnitude of that gap or directly test any other listed version. Numbers from figures are not reconstructed.
record.test_reason: The study measures effective information from interventions on node activations, not magnitude-aware weight sharpness or its ranking of generalization gaps. Its own results test none of V1–V8; the proposed connection between causal-structure differentiation and generalization remains a hypothesis.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: EI and its sensitivity and degeneracy components characterize changes in network causal structure during training. The authors hypothesize that causal-structure differentiation may help explain generalization; they do not establish that relationship.
record.recipe_differences: Measures information-theoretic causal-structure trajectories during training rather than magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness and its relation to generalization-gap rankings.
record.method_sensitivity: Activation function changes precise EI behavior; reduced-MNIST and Iris tasks show different degrees of causal-plane differentiation.

fits_no_version.finding: EI changes most during steep loss reductions and is generally flat when training and testing performance diverge.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Activation-intervention effective information changes during learning but can remain stable during overfitting in the tested small networks.

fits_no_version.finding: EI trajectories are broadly similar across activation functions, with differences in their precise behavior.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The qualitative training dynamics of effective information persist across sigmoid, tanh, and ReLU in the tested networks.

record.code_released: repository referenced as publicly available; URL not stated in supplied text
record.problems: The study does not directly measure or quantify generalization gaps as a function of EI or compare EI with sharpness, norm, or margin measures. Results are based on three runs per task for the main experiments; exact curve values are presented in figures without numerical tables.
record.rows_left_out: None. Figure-only numeric values were not reconstructed; the corresponding described findings are captured in R1–R4.

untested.parts: Random-label memorization, natural-label generalization, and chance performance on held-out random labels.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization under different tuning regimes.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that reduce their penalty.
Dropout effects on held-out error and their dependence on data size, strength, and other regularization.
Magnitude-aware weight-perturbation sharpness, its association with generalization gaps among similarly fitted networks, and comparisons with norm- and margin-based rankings.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Flat EI during overfitting neither challenges nor limits V7 because EI is a different construct from magnitude-aware sharpness. The existing V7 verdicts should be removed.

versions.untested_parts: Memorization of random labels and generalization on natural labels.
Width sweeps beyond interpolation and their effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the role of local connectivity.
Large-batch versus small-batch training and recipe adaptations.
Dropout and weight-decay effects on held-out error.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness, comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures, CIFAR-10/SVHN settings, and the claim that this measure ranks generalization gaps better.
Removing memorized examples and measuring resulting test accuracy.

rows.subject: Iris networks (4 → 5 → 5 → 3)
rows.operation_detail: Tracked effective information (EI) by layer during training alongside training and testing MSE loss.
rows.measure: Whether EI changes during learning and during the period when training performance dissociates from testing performance.
rows.value: The greatest EI changes significantly match the steepest parts of the loss curve; during overfitting, EI was generally flat across all layers.
rows.note: The paper describes loss curves and EI trajectories, but does not quantify the training–test error gap or show that EI ranks gap sizes.
rows.check: EI trajectories cannot establish V7's sharpness–gap relationship. The reported correspondence with loss changes is qualitative; no statistical significance test is reported.
